title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Oil fell almost 6% on Monday to its lowest since August after Trump said he would hold off new strikes on Iran, but the US blockade of Hormuz stays and ship attacks go on. DHL is moving freight capacity to the UAE east coast, and Saudi air links are still patchy.

gauges.label: Brent crude settle, Monday
gauges.note: Down 5.85% to the lowest since 31 August; $92.33 early Tuesday (Reuters via Business Recorder, 10 Nov)

gauges.label: Hormuz traffic vs pre-war
gauges.note: Still the latest figure (Lloyd's List Intelligence via The National, 8 Nov); US blockade stays for now

stories.headline: Trump holds off new Iran strikes but keeps the Hormuz blockade
body: Trump said on Monday he will hold off new military strikes on Iran for now, after appeals from regional countries including Qatar's prime minister. He said the US naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz stays in place for now.

Attacks on ships near Hormuz are still happening but "have not escalated", said KCM Trade's Tim Waterer. Senior US and Gulf officials doubt a peace deal is close, and Iran's Mohsen Rezaei told the US to stop talking about "imaginary talks".
stories.soWhat: New since Monday: the strike threat is lower, but the blockade and the attacks are not over. Sea war-risk pricing stays; do not promise customers relief yet.

stories.headline: Saudi air links: Dammam reopens for flydubai, Riyadh still largely cut
body: flydubai's schedule shows Dubai–Dammam from today, 10 November, with Riyadh and Abha from 17 November. Etihad has cancelled all Abu Dhabi–Riyadh and Dammam passenger and cargo flights through 19 November. SalamAir is off both cities until 30 November.

Emirates is unclear: The National reported Riyadh and Dammam restarting on 8 November, but AeroCorner found Emirates' own system still showing those flights cancelled through 13 November. Saudi air defences intercepted two Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh on 8 November.
stories.soWhat: New: Dammam belly space is back today, but Riyadh air stays unreliable. Keep Riyadh on road and confirm uplift before every promise.
stories.source: Khaleej Times; The National; AeroCorner; Gulf News

stories.headline: Oil drops almost 6% to a two-month low
body: Brent settled at $92.57 on Monday, down $5.75 or 5.85%, its lowest since 31 August. It was at $92.33 early on Tuesday. WTI was at $86.50. On Friday Brent had closed at $98.29.
Reuters says Middle East producers are cutting prices to attract buyers as Hormuz oil flows recover, raising oversupply worries. OPEC output rose in October, led by Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq.
stories.soWhat: Fuel costs are easing for the first time in weeks. If it holds, customers will ask for December surcharge cuts; decide our rule now.

competitors.name: DHL
competitors.headline: Builds up in the eastern UAE near Khor Fakkan and Dibba; keeps €500m Gulf spend
body: DHL Global Forwarding will strengthen its position in the eastern UAE, near Khor Fakkan and Dibba in Fujairah. MEA CEO Tobias Maier told The National its €500 million Gulf commitment is unchanged, after earlier facilities worth €120 million in the UAE and €130 million in Saudi Arabia, plus a 20-year joint venture with Etihad Rail.
Maier said the industry will need three to six months to normalise after the conflict ends, and that higher freight rates are "normal" for this market.
competitors.soWhat: DHL is locking in the Hormuz bypass and rail. It is also telling shippers rates normalise in 3–6 months, faster than our CEO's 6–12; expect it to price for that.

competitors.name: Emirates SkyCargo
competitors.headline: Still holding Riyadh and Dammam back while rivals return
body: Emirates' own flight-status system showed Dubai–Riyadh and Dubai–Dammam flights cancelled every day from 8 to 13 November, when AeroCorner checked on 6 November, despite reports of an 8 November restart. Etihad has cancelled its Riyadh and Dammam cargo and passenger flights through 19 November.
competitors.soWhat: The two big UAE carriers are still off the main Saudi lanes. Our road network to Riyadh is the product to sell this week.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: CEO targets double-digit growth; sees rates easing 6–12 months after peace
body: Group CEO Amadou Diallo told Khaleej Times Aramex aims for double-digit revenue growth in 2026 and 2027, and that freight rates should normalise six to 12 months after peace returns. Q2 revenue was a record Dh1.83 billion, up 22%, and net profit rose seven-fold to Dh47 million. Aramex is piloting drones for middle-mile deliveries.
competitors.soWhat: Our public view of the rate cycle is slower than DHL's. Sales need one clear message on when customers will see rates fall.

opportunities.title: Dubai–Dammam air is back
opportunities.text: flydubai flies Dammam from today. Call shippers who moved to road and offer air again.

opportunities.title: UAE–Riyadh road freight
opportunities.text: Etihad is off Riyadh to 19 November and Emirates is unclear. Keep selling trucking on the lane.

opportunities.title: East-coast gateways
opportunities.text: DHL is building near Khor Fakkan and Dibba. Package east-coast port plus trucking into Dubai before it locks in shippers.

opportunities.title: Fuel relief as a retention tool
opportunities.text: Brent is down almost 6%. A clear, rule-based surcharge cut can win renewals with key accounts.

watchouts.title: Oil whipsaw
watchouts.text: One day down 5.85%. Iran denies any talks and the blockade stays. Prices can jump back fast.

watchouts.title: Rate-cut pressure
watchouts.text: DHL says the market normalises 3–6 months after the war. Customers will use that against our rates.

watchouts.title: DHL east-coast build-out
watchouts.text: €500m Gulf spend, an Etihad Rail joint venture and now Khor Fakkan and Dibba.

watchouts.title: Saudi air schedule confusion
watchouts.text: Emirates' system shows Riyadh and Dammam cancelled to 13 November. Do not promise Saudi air without confirmed uplift.

watchouts.title: Missiles at Riyadh
watchouts.text: Two Houthi missiles were intercepted over Riyadh on 8 November. Air links can close again.

moves.title: Set a fuel surcharge trigger
moves.text: Brent dropped to $92.57. Agree now what level and for how long cuts the December surcharge, so we move first.

moves.title: Keep sea war-risk surcharges
moves.text: The Hormuz blockade stays and attacks continue. No cuts on Gulf sea lanes yet.

moves.title: Prepare a post-war rate path
moves.text: DHL is selling 3–6 months to normal. Give key accounts our own step-down plan before they ask.

moves.title: Sell east-coast routings
moves.text: Offer Khor Fakkan and Fujairah entry with trucking to Dubai, ahead of DHL's build-out.

moves.title: Confirm Dammam uplift today
moves.text: Book flydubai Dammam space for express; keep Riyadh on road until airlines confirm.

note: Read from today's news. Check against our own numbers before acting.
